In [[mathematics]], the '''Bogomolov conjecture''' is a conjecture, named after [[Fedor Bogomolov]],<ref>{{cite journal|last1 = Bogomolov| first1 = Fedor| journal = Math. USSR, Izv.|volume=17|year=1981|pages=55–72|title=Points of finite order on an Abelian variety}}</ref> in [[arithmetic geometry]] about [[algebraic curve]]s that generalizes the [[Manin–Mumford conjecture]] in [[arithmetic geometry]].

The conjecture was proven by [[Emmanuel Ullmo]] in 1998 <ref name="Ullmo-1998">{{Citation |last=Ullmo |first=Emmanuel |title=Positivité et Discrétion des Points Algébriques des Courbes |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=147 |issue=1 |year=1998 |pages=167–179 |doi=10.2307/120987 |jstor=120987 | zbl=0934.14013 |arxiv=alg-geom/9606017 }}.</ref> and was subsequently generalized by [[Shou-Wu Zhang]] to [[Algebraic varieties|subvarieties]] of general [[abelian varieties]] in 1998.<ref name="Zhang-1998">{{Citation |last=Zhang|first=S.-W. |title=Equidistribution of small points on abelian varieties |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=147 |issue=1 |year=1998 |pages=159–165 |doi=10.2307/120986|jstor=120986 }}</ref> Both Ullmo's and Zhang's proofs rely on [[Arakelov theory]]. The idea of using Arakelov theory to attack the Bogomolov conjecture is due to [[Lucien Szpiro]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1 = Szpiro|first1=Lucien|journal=Progress in Mathematics|title=Sur les proprietes numeriques du dualisant relatif d'une surface arithmetique|year=1990|issue=88|pages=229–246}}</ref>

In recent years, generalizations and variants of the Bogomolov conjecture have become a central area of research in both [[arithmetic dynamics]] and [[diophantine geometry]], motivating many developments in both fields.

==Manin-Mumford conjecture==
The [[Manin-Mumford conjecture]] concerns the finiteness of [[Torsion (algebra)#Abelian varieties|torsion points]] lying on an algebraic curve <math>C</math> of [[genus (mathematics)|genus]] <math>g \geq 2</math>, over a [[field (mathematics)|field]] <math> K</math> of [[Characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] zero, when the curve is embedded into its [[Jacobian variety]]. The conjecture was independently formulated by [[Yuri Manin]] and [[David Mumford]], and was inspired by [[André Weil]]'s approach to the [[Mordell's conjecture]] (also known as [[Gerd Faltings|Faltings']] theorem).<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Lang | first1 = Serge | journal = Encyclopedia of Mathematical Sciences| title = Number Theory III: Diophantine Geometry| volume=60| year=1991}}</ref>

More generally, in the spirit of the [[Bombieri-Lang conjecture]], one may ask when does an irreducible subvariety <math>V</math> of an abelian variety <math>A</math> have a [[Zariski topology|Zariski dense]] set of torsion points. The Manin-Mumford conjecture asserts that this occurs if and only if <math>V </math> is a torsion [[coset]], that is, <math>V</math> is of the form <math>x+B</math> where <math>B</math> is an abelian subvariety of <math>A</math> and <math>x</math> a torsion point of <math>A</math>.

The Manin-Mumford conjecture, both for curves embedded in Jacobians and for general subvarieties of abelian varieties, was proven by [[Michel Raynaud]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Raynaud| first1 = Michel| journal = Inventiones| title = Courbes sur une varietie abelienne et points de torsion| volume=71| year=1983 |pages=207–233}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Raynaud| first1 = Michel| journal = Progress in Mathematics| title = Sous-varieties d'une varietie abelienne et points de torsion| volume=35| year=1983 |pages=327–352}}</ref>  Alternative proofs and further generalizations were later obtained by [[Jean-Pierre Serre]], Marc Hindry <ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Hindry| first1 = Marc| journal = Inventiones| title = Autour d'une conjecture de Serge Lang | volume=94(3)| year=1988 |pages=575–603}}</ref> and [[Robert F. Coleman|Robert Coleman]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Coleman| first1 = Robert| journal = Duke Mathematical Journal| title = Ramified torsion points on curves| volume=43| year=1983 |pages=207–233}}</ref>

When <math>K</math> is of characteristic <math>p</math>, additional assumptions on <math>A</math> are needed for the Manin-Mumford conjecture to hold because of the presence of the [[Frobenius endomorphism]]. Special cases were proven by [[Dan Abramovich]] and [[José Felipe Voloch]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Abramovich| first1 = Dan| last2 = Voloch | first2 = José Felipe | journal = IMRN| title = Towards a proof of the Mordell-Lang conjecture in characteristic <math>p</math>| volume=5| year=1992 |pages=103–115}}</ref> Using ideas from [[model theory]], [[Ehud Hrushovski]] later proved a general version for the prime-to-<math>p</math> torsion group.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Hrushovski| first1 = Ehud| journal = Journal of the American Mathematical Society| title = The Mordell-Lang conjecture for function fields| volume=9(3)| year=1996 |pages=667–690}}</ref> This was subsequently extended by Richard Pink and Damian Rössler to the full torsion group.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Pink| first1 = Richard| last2 = Rössler | first2=Damian| journal = Journal of Algebraic Geometry| title = On <math>\psi</math>-invariant subvarieties of semiabelian varieties and the Manin-Mumford conjecture| volume=13(4)| year=2004 |pages=771–798}}</ref>

The Manin-Mumford conjecture can be viewed as a special case of the [[Zilber-Pink conjecture]]. The Zilber-Pink conjecture remains widely open.

==Bogomolov conjecture==
The Bogomolov conjecture generalizes the Manin-Mumford conjecture by replacing torsion points with points of small [[Néron-Tate height]]. More precisely, let <math>C</math> be a curve of genus <math>g \geq 2</math> that is defined over a number field <math>K</math>. Let <math>L</math> be a symmetric [[ample line bundle]] for the Jacobian <math>J</math> and let <math>\widehat{h}</math> denote the associated Néron-Tate height on <math>J</math>. The Bogomolov conjecture predicts there exists <math>\epsilon > 0</math> such that the set 
{{center| <math>\{ x \in C(\overline{K}) : \widehat{h}(x) < \epsilon\}</math>}} 
is finite. Since <math>\widehat{h}(x) = 0 </math> if and only if <math>x</math> is a torsion point, this recovers the Manin-Mumford conjecture as a special case. Heuristically, points of small Néron-Tate height may be viewed as arithmetic analogues of points lying "close" to torsion points. From this perspective, the Bogomolov conjecture predicts that the finiteness phenomenon of Manin–Mumford persists even after replacing each torsion point by a small arithmetic neighborhood.

Much like the Manin-Mumford conjecture, the Bogomolov conjecture extends naturally to arbitrary subvarieties <math>V \subseteq A </math> of an abelian variety. In this more general setting, the conjecture predicts that if <math>V</math> is not a torsion coset, then there exists <math>\epsilon>0</math> such that 
{{center| <math>\{ x \in V(\overline{K}) : \widehat{h}(x) < \epsilon\}</math>}} 
is not Zariski dense in <math>V</math>.

The Bogomolov conjecture for curves embedded in their Jacobians was proven by Ullmo using equidistribution of [[Conjugate element (field theory)|Galois orbits]] of points with small [[Néron-Tate height]] towards the [[Haar measure]] of the abelian variety.<ref name="Ullmo-1998" /> This equidistribution phenomenon was established by [[Lucien Szpiro]], Ullmo and Zhang  through methods of [[Arakelov theory]],<ref>{{cite journal|last1 = Szpiro|first1 = Lucien | last2= Ullmo | first2 = Emmanuel | last3 = Zhang | first3 = Shou-Wu| journal=Inventiones |title= Equidistribution of Small Points|issue=127 |year=1998|pages=337–347}}</ref> using the arithmetic [[Riemann-Roch]] theorem developed by [[Henri Gillet]] and [[Christophe Soulé]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1 = Gillet|first1 = Henri | last2= Soulé | first2 = Christophe | journal=Inventiones |title= An arithmetic Riemann-Roch theorem|issue=110(3) |year=1992|pages=473–543}}</ref> The general case of [[Algebraic varieties|subvarieties]] of [[abelian variety|abelian varieties]] was proven by Zhang using equidistribution too.<ref name = "Zhang-1998" />

An alternative proof of the Bogomolov conjecture for subvarieties was obtained by Sinnou David and Patrice Philippon using techniques from [[diophantine approximation]] and [[transcendental number theory]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1 = David|first1 = Sinnou | last2 = Philippon | first2= David | journal=Commentarii Mathematici Helvetici|title=Minorations des hautuers normalises des sous-varieties de varieties abeliennes. II|issue=183(3) |year=2011|pages=517–562}}</ref> Their approach is quantitative in nature, yielding an explicit <math>\epsilon > 0 </math> together with an upper bound for the degree of a subvariety containing all points of height at most <math>\epsilon</math>.

==Geometric Bogomolov conjecture==
As the Néron-Tate height can be defined over any field <math>K</math> that has a [[height function|Weil height function]], the Bogomolov conjecture admits a natural extension to more general fields. When <math>K</math> is the [[function field of an algebraic variety]], this statement is known as the geometric Bogomolov conjecture. Building on earlier work of Zhang,<ref>{{cite journal|last1 = Zhang|first1 = Shou-Wu | journal=Inventiones|title=Admissible pairing on a curve|issue=112(1) |year=1993|pages=171–193}}</ref> Atsushi Moriwaki,<ref>{{cite journal|last1 = Moriwaki|first1 = Atsushi | journal=Journal of Mathematics of Kyoto University|title= Bogomolov conjecture for curves of genus 2 over function fields|issue=36(4) |year=1996|pages=687–695}}</ref> Kazuhiko Yamaki <ref>{{cite journal|last1 = Yamaki|first1 = Kazuhiko | journal=Journal of Mathematics of Kyoto University|title= Geometric Bogomolov's conjecture for curves of genus 3 over function fields|issue=42(1) |year=2002|pages=57–81}}</ref> and Xander Faber <ref>{{cite journal|last1 = Faber|first1 = Xander| journal=Experimental Mathematics|title= The Geometric Bogomolov  conjecture for curves of small genus|issue=18(3) |year=2009|pages=347–367}}</ref> prove the conjecture for low genus curves embedded in their Jacobians using [[potential theory]] on [[Graph theory|graphs]]. The general case was settled by Zubeyir Cinkir.<ref>{{cite journal|last1 = Cinkir|first1 = Zubeyir | journal=Inventiones|title=Zhang's conjecture and the effective Bogomolov conjecture over function fields|issue=183(3) |year=2011|pages=517–562}}</ref>

For higher dimensional subvarieties over function fields <math>K</math>, Zhang's approach is difficult to carry over due to the lack of an [[archimedean place]]. To overcome this, Antoine Chambert-Loir introduced canonical measures on [[Berkovich space]]s as [[non-archimedean field|non-archimedean]] analogues of the measures appearing in Szpiro-Ullmo-Zhang's equidistribution theorem.<ref>{{cite journal|last1 = Chambert-Loir|first1 = Antoine | journal=J. Reine Angew. Math.|title= Measures and equidistribution in Berkovich spaces|issue=595 |year=2006|pages=215–235}}</ref> In a series of works, Walter Gubler proved that Galois orbits of small points do equidistribute to this Chambert-Loir measure <ref>{{cite journal|last1 = Gubler|first1 = Walter | journal=Manuscripta Mathematica|title= Equidistribution over function fields|issue=127(4) |year=2008|pages=485–510}}</ref> and studied its properties using [[tropical geometry]],<ref>{{cite journal|last1 = Gubler|first1 = Walter | journal=Inventiones|title= Tropical varieties for non-archimedean analytic spaces|issue=169(2) |year=2007|pages=321–376}}</ref> leading to a proof of the Bogomolov conjecture when <math>A</math> has a place of totally degenerate reduction.<ref>{{cite journal|last1 = Gubler|first1 = Walter | journal=Inventiones|title= The Bogomolov conjecture for totally degenerate abelian varieties|issue=169(2) |year=2007|pages=377–400}}</ref> The full geometric Bogomolov conjecture was resolved by Junyi Xie and [[Xinyi Yuan]] by reducing it to the Manin-Mumford conjecture.<ref>{{cite journal|last1 = Xie|first1 = Junyi | last2= Yuan | first2 = Xinyi| journal=Inventiones|title=Geometric Bogomolov conjecture in arbitrary characteristics|issue=229(2)|year=2022|pages=607–637}}</ref> Their proof uses a reduction argument due to Yamaki to the case where <math>A</math> has everywhere good reduction.<ref>{{cite journal|last1 = Yamaki|first1 = Kazuhiko | journal=J. Reine Angew. Math.|title=Trace of abelian varieties over function fields and the geometric {Bogomolov} conjecture|issue=741|year=2018|pages=133–159}}</ref>

When <math>K</math> is the function field of a curve with characteristic zero, [[Ziyang Gao]] and [[Philipp Habegger]] gave an alternative proof using methods from [[o-minimal theory|o-minimality]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1 = Gao|first1 = Ziyang | last2= Habegger | first2 = Philipp| journal=Annals of Mathematics|title=Heights in families of abelian varieties and the geometric Bogomolov conjecture|issue=189(2)|year=2019|pages=527–604}}</ref>  This was extended to general characteristic zero function fields by [[Serge Cantat]], Gao, Habegger and Xie, where they replace the o-minimality arguments with [[ergodic theory]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1 = Cantat|first1 = Serge | last2= Gao | first2 = Ziyang| last3=Habegger|first3=Philipp|last4=Xie|first4=Junyi | journal=Duke Mathematical Journal|title=The geometric Bogomolov conjecture|issue=170(2)|year=2021|pages=247–277}}</ref>

For arithmetic function fields, the Bogomolov conjecture was proven by Moriwaki.<ref>{{cite journal|last1 = Moriwaki|first1 = Atsushi| journal=Inventiones|title=Arithmetic height functions over finitely generated fields|issue=140(1)|year=2000|pages=101–142}}</ref>

==Uniform variants==
The uniform Manin-Mumford conjecture for curves embedded in their Jacobians, proposed by [[Barry Mazur]],<ref>{{cite journal| last1= Mazur| first1 = Barry | journal = Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|title=Arithmetic on curves| volume=14|year=1986|pages=209–259}}</ref> predicts the existence of a constant <math>N = N(g)> 0</math>, depending only on the genus <math>g</math> of our algebraic curve <math>C</math>, such that <math>C</math> contains at most <math>N</math> torsion points of its Jacobian.

Analogously, one may formulate a uniform Bogomolov conjecture: there should exists constants <math>\epsilon = \epsilon(g) > 0</math> and <math>N = N(g) > 0</math>, depending only on <math>g</math> and not on the curve <math>C</math> or number field <math>K</math>, such that the set
{{center| <math>\{ x \in C(\overline{K}) : \widehat{h}(x) < \epsilon\}</math>}} 
contains at most <math>N</math> points.

Special cases of the uniform Bogomolov conjecture were established by David and Phillipon,<ref>{{cite journal| last1= David| first1 = Sinnou | last2 = Phillipon |first2 = Patrice| journal = International Mathematics Research Papers|title= Lower bounds of normalized heights of subvarieties of powers of elliptic curves|year=2007|page=113}}</ref> and later by [[Laura DeMarco]], [[Holly Krieger]] and Hexi Ye.<ref name="DKY-1">{{cite journal|last1=DeMarco|first1=Laura|last2=Krieger|first2=Holly|last3=Ye|first3=Hexi|journal=Annals of Mathematics |title=Uniform Manin-Mumford for a family of genus 2 curves|issue=191(3)|year=2020|pages=949–1001}}</ref> David and Phillipon further conjectured that the constant <math>\epsilon</math> may be replaced with <math> \epsilon \max\{h_{\mathrm{Fal}}(C),1\} </math>, where <math>h_{\mathrm{Fal}}(C)</math> denotes the Faltings height of <math>C</math>.

When <math>h_{\mathrm{Fal}}(C) </math> is sufficiently large, [[Vesselin Dimitrov]], Gao and Habegger proved this strengthened form by studying the non-degeneracy of families of curves.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Dimitrov|first1=Vesselin|last2=Gao|first2=Ziyang|last3=Habegger|first3=Phillip|journal=Annals of Mathematics |title=Uniformity in Mordell-Lang for curves|issue=194(1)|year=2021|pages=237–298}}</ref> Combined with Gaël Remond's quantitative refinement of [[Paul Vojta|Vojta's]] inequality,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Remond|first1=Gaël |journal=Ann. Sc. Norm. Super. Pisa, Cl. Sci., IV. Ser. |title=Vojta's inequality in higher dimension|issue=29(1)|year=2000|pages=101–151}}</ref> their work implies the existence of a constant <math>c = c(g,K) > 0</math>, depending on the genus <math>g</math> and the number field <math>K</math> that the size of <math>C(K)</math> is bounded by <math>c^{\mathrm{rk}\,J(K) + 1}</math>, where <math>\mathrm{rk}</math> <math>J(K)</math> denotes the rank of the [[Mordell-Weil theorem|Mordell-Weil group]] of <math>J(K)</math>. This yields a uniform version of the Mordell conjecture and a proof of [[Uniform boundedness conjecture for rational points#Mazur's conjecture B|Mazur's conjecture B]].

The full uniform Bogomolov conjecture for curves in their Jacobians was proven by Lars Kühne,<ref>{{cite web|last1=Kühne|first1=Lars|title = Equidistribution in Families of Abelian Varieties and Uniformity
|year=2024|url=https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.10272}}</ref> building on the work of Dimitrov, Gao and Habegger. Subsequently, Tangli Ge, Gao and Kühne proved the uniform Bogomolov conjecture for higher dimensional subvarieties.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Ge|first1=Tangli|last2=Gao|first2=Ziyang|last3=Kühne |first3=Lars|title = The Uniform Mordell-Lang Conjecture
|year=2021|url=https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.15085}}</ref> An alternative proof in the case of curves in Jacobians was given by Yuan, based on the theory of adelic line bundles over quasi-projective varieties by Yuan and Zhang.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Yuan|first1=Xinyi|title=Arithmetic bigness and a uniform Bogomolov-type result|year=2021|url=https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.05625}}</ref>

Over function fields, a quantitative form of the uniform Bogomolov conjecture for curves in Jacobians was proven by Nicole Looper, [[Joseph H. Silverman|Joseph Silverman]] and Robert Wilms.<ref>{{cite journal|journal= J. Reine Angew. Math.|last1=Looper|first1=Nicole|last2=Silverman|first2=Joseph|last3=Wilms |first3=Robert|title = A uniform quantitative Manin-Mumford theorem for curves over function fields
|year=2025|issue=828|pages=127–147}}</ref> Over number fields, Yuan, Jiawei Yu and Shengxuan Zhou established a quantitative version for curves in Jacobians, which yields a quantitative version of the uniform Mordell conjecture.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Yuan|first1=Xinyi|last2=Yu|first2=Jiawei|last3=Zhou|first3=Shengxuan|title=Quantitavity on the number of rational points in the Mordell conjecture|year=2026|url=https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.01820}}</ref>

==Dynamical Variants==
Motivated by Silverman's dictionary between [[arithmetic dynamics]] and diophantine geometry, Zhang proposed a dynamical generalization of the Manin-Mumford conjecture, known as the dynamical Manin-Mumford conjecture.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Zhang|first1=Shou-Wu|title=Distributions in algebraic dynamics|journal=Surveys in Differential Geometry|issue=10|pages=381–430|year=2006}}</ref> Let <math>f: X \to X </math> be an [[endomorphism]] of a [[projective variety]] that is polarizable, which is to say there exists an ample line bundle <math>L</math> and <math>d > 1</math> such that <math>f^* L \simeq L^{\otimes d}</math>. Then the conjecture asserts that if <math>V \subseteq X</math> is a subvariety containing a Zariski dense set of [[periodic point|preperiodic]] points, then <math>V</math> itself is preperiodic.

This formulation of the dynamical Manin-Mumford conjecture turned out to be false, with counterexamples coming from [[elliptic curves]] with [[complex multiplication]]. Dragos Ghioca, Thomas Tucker and Zhang fixed the conjecture by weakening the conclusion that <math>V</math> is preperiodic.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Ghioca|first1=Dragos|last2=Tucker|first2=Thomas|last3=Zhang|first3=Shou-Wu|title=Towards a dynamical Manin-Mumford conjecture|year=2011|journal=IMRN|volume=22|pages=5109–5122}}</ref>

One can also formulate a dynamical Bogomolov conjecture by replacing the Néron-Tate height with the [[Néron–Tate height#Call-Silverman Canonical Height|Call-Silverman canonical height]].

For <math>X = (\mathbb{P}^1)^n</math> and <math>f</math> a split endomorphism, the dynamical Manin-Mumford and Bogomolov conjectures were proven by Dragos Ghioca, Dang-Khoa Nguyen and Hexi Ye.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Ghioca|first1=Dragos|last2=Nguyen|first2=Dang-Khoa|last3=Ye|first3=Hexi|title=The dynamical Manin-Mumford conjecture and the dynamical Bogomolov conjecture for endomorphisms on (\mathbb{P}^1)^n|journal = Compositio Mathematica|year=2018|issue=154(7)|pages=1441–1472}}</ref> Both conjectures remain wide open for <math>X = \mathbb{P}^n</math> where <math>n \geq 2 </math>. Special cases were proven by Romain Dujardin and Charles Favre,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Dujardin|first1=Romain|last2=Favre|first2=Charles|title=The dynamical Manin-Mumford problem for plane polynomial automorphisms|journal=Journal of the European Mathematical Society|year=2017|issue=19(11)|pages=3421–3465}}</ref> and by Dujardin, Favre and Matteo Ruggiero.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Dujardin|first1=Romain|last2=Favre|first2=Charles|last3=Ruggiero|first3=Matteo|title=On the dynamical Manin-Mumford conjecture for plane polynomial maps
|year=2023|url=https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.14817}}</ref>

Uniform versions were proven by DeMarco, Krieger and Ye for the case of <math>X = (\mathbb{P}^1)^2, V = \Delta</math> is the diagonal, and <math>(f,g)</math> belonging to either the family of [[Adrien-Marie Legendre|Legendre]] [[Lattès map]]s<ref name="DKY-1" /> or [[Complex quadratic polynomial|quadratic unicritical polynomials]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=DeMarco|first1=Laura|last2=Krieger|first2=Holly|last3=Ye|first3=Hexi|journal=Journal of Modern Dynamics |title=Common preperiodic points for quadratic polynomials|issue=18|year=2022|pages=363–413}}</ref> The case of general Lattès maps was settled later by Jérôme Poineau, which settled the Bogomolov-Fu-[[Yuri Tschinkel|Tschinkel]] conjecture.<ref>{{cite web|last1= Poineau|first1=Jérôme|title=Dynamique analytique sur <math>\mathbb{Z}</math> II : Écart uniforme entre Lattès et conjecture de Bogomolov-Fu-Tschinkel|year=2025|url=https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.01574}}</ref> Uniformity in one parameter families for <math>X = (\mathbb{P}^1)^2</math> and <math>V_t</math> any one-parameter family of curves was proven by Niki Myrto Mavraki and Harry Schmidt.<ref>{{cite journal|journal = Duke Mathematical Journal|last1=Mavraki|first1=Niki Myrto|last2= Schmidt|first2=Harry|title=On the dynamical Bogomolov conjecture for families of split rational maps|year=2025|issue=174(5)|pages=803–856}}</ref>
